title: One-dollar price rise for a managed service in one region
question: What could happen if AWS increases the price of a particular cloud service by $1 in a selected region?

participants.name: Company leadership
participants.rationale: Somebody decides how the company responds; no source names who.

participants.name: Head of finance

quote.text: The head of finance wants a range for the annual cost and a view on whether the company's committed-spend discount would apply to the increase.

participants.rationale: Owns the cost range and the discount question.

quote.text: Engineering managers have been asked whether workloads could run in Region S or with another provider, and at what effort.
The sales director is concerned about customers that renewed at fixed prices last quarter.
Customers on monthly plans, mostly small retailers, can leave with 30 days' notice.
Public-sector customers and large retailers negotiate renewals through procurement teams and usually ask for a written justification of any rise.

participants.name: Customers with data-residency contracts

quote.text: Eleven customers have contracts naming that jurisdiction as the place where their data must stay, so their workloads could not move without each customer's agreement.

participants.rationale: Their workloads cannot move without agreement.

participants.name: Audit committee and external auditors

quote.text: The audit committee of the board has asked for a written note on supplier concentration, and the external auditors have raised the same point.

participants.rationale: Ask for a note on supplier concentration.

participants.name: Cloud reseller

quote.text: The company's cloud reseller has offered a call about commitment options.

participants.rationale: Relays the notice and offers commitment options.

quote.text: It says that the provider is raising the price of the service in Region R by one dollar and that details are to follow.

participants.name: Rival analytics vendors

quote.text: Three rival analytics vendors sell to the same retailers.

participants.rationale: Sell to the same retailers; two advertise price locks.

participants.name: Implementation partners

quote.text: Implementation partners who resell the product keep 15% of subscription revenue.

participants.rationale: Resell the product and must explain any rise.

quote.text: Gross margin on the analytics product is 71%, and investors and the board follow it each quarter.
Support engineers expect more incidents during any cut-over, especially for customers on shared accounts.

participants.name: Migration consultancy

quote.text: A consultancy that has offered migration services estimates that moving the service's workloads out of Region R would take 4 engineer-months.

participants.rationale: Would earn fees from a move.

participants.name: Retailers' own shoppers
participants.rationale: Reached through the retailers; no source mentions them.

constraints.quote: Most customer-facing workloads run in Region R because several customers require their data to stay in that jurisdiction.
Eleven customers have contracts naming that jurisdiction as the place where their data must stay, so their workloads could not move without each customer's agreement.
Pass-through clauses, which let the company raise prices after a supplier increase, exist in a minority of contracts, and some require 60 days' notice.
constraints.rationale: A notice period in some contracts.

constraints.quote: Region S has less spare capacity for the service than Region R, so a quota increase would have to be requested, and the provider's response time is unknown.
constraints.rationale: A move needs quota the provider has to grant.

constraints.quote: The security team notes that a second provider would need its own review, and reviews of earlier suppliers took about five months.
constraints.rationale: A required review with a known duration.

constraints.quote: It gives no effective date, does not say whether committed-spend agreements or reserved capacity are affected and does not name the billing unit for the one-dollar figure.
constraints.rationale: The notice leaves key terms open.

constraints.quote: The agreement summary the company holds does not say whether the discount would apply to an increase.
The audit committee of the board has asked for a written note on supplier concentration, and the external auditors have raised the same point.
Public-sector customers and large retailers negotiate renewals through procurement teams and usually ask for a written justification of any rise.
Customers on monthly plans, mostly small retailers, can leave with 30 days' notice.

gap.removeText: Region S has less spare capacity for the service than Region R, so a quota increase would have to be requested, and the provider's response time is unknown.
gap.rationale: The only statement about spare capacity in Region S.

alternatives.rationale: Run workloads in the secondary region.
Commitment options offered by the reseller.

claims.statement: A $1 increase in Region R would add $18,400 a month at list price, or $220,800 a year, before any discount.
The platform team estimates that moving the service's workloads out of Region R would take 9 engineer-months.
Fixed-price contracts cover 38% of annual recurring revenue.
The provider has announced that the price rise takes effect next quarter.
claims.rationale: The notice gives no effective date.

claims.statement: A second provider would be cheaper for the company's workloads.
claims.rationale: Nobody has tried another provider with these volumes.

claims.statement: Eleven customers have contracts that require their data to stay in the Region R jurisdiction.

a.quote: Finance counts fixed-price contracts as covering 38% of annual recurring revenue.

b.quote: Sales operations counts fixed-price contracts as covering 55% of annual recurring revenue.

conflicts.rationale: Two shares for the same count.

a.quote: The platform team estimates that moving the service's workloads out of Region R would take 9 engineer-months.

b.quote: A consultancy that has offered migration services estimates that moving the service's workloads out of Region R would take 4 engineer-months.

conflicts.rationale: Two estimates of the same work.
